verdict.rationale: Keycloak's own docs say social login is added in the admin console by selecting the social network, with "No code or changes to your application" needed. Any external OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0 identity provider can also be configured the same way. Hands-on users confirm Google SSO "was a few settings away" and that they "integrated a lot of external IdP's". Missing for 10: an enumerated list of the built-in social providers proving how broad the set is, and in-depth first-party identity-brokering setup docs beyond marketing-page statements.

support.subject: As a developer, I can offer sign-in with a broad set of social and OAuth identity providers through configuration, not custom code

citations.quote: Enabling login with social networks is easy to add through the admin console. It's just a matter of selecting the social network you want to add. No code or changes to your application is required.
Keycloak can also authenticate users with existing OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0 Identity Providers. Again, this is just a matter of configuring the Identity Provider through the admin console.
Google SSO was a few settings away
integrated a lot of external IdP's to offer proper SSO on multiple of our software stacks
